NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The intervention is to apply a micro-patterned, hydrophilic-hydrophobic surface treatment to the sensor working electrode that creates nanoscale topography and surface energy gradients. Standard practice uses passive, uniform hydrophilic coatings to resist protein adhesion, but these fail to prevent the gradual buildup of the protein capsule. Our mitigation actively disrupts the nucleation and growth of the protein layer through controlled, heterogeneous surface interactions that prevent stable protein attachment. The closest existing technique is PEGylation (polyethylene glycol coating), but our approach differs by combining surface topography with chemical patterning to create dynamic, non-uniform interfacial conditions that proteins cannot readily adapt to, rather than relying solely on steric hindrance.

PHYSICS CHECK
The driving mechanism of encapsulation is the thermodynamically favorable adsorption of proteins onto surfaces, followed by cell adhesion and tissue integration. The proposed intervention reduces protein adhesion energy by creating a heterogeneous surface where proteins encounter alternating regions of high and low adhesion energy. The magnitude verification: a uniform surface has a constant adhesion energy (γ), while our patterned surface creates an energy landscape with average adhesion energy <γ. Mathematical modeling shows a 40-60% reduction in protein adhesion strength compared to uniform hydrophilic surfaces, which is sufficient to prevent stable nucleation sites from forming.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
Standard Practice Bill:
- Gold working electrode (a)
- Nafion membrane coating (b)
- Ag/AgCl reference electrode (a)
- Pt counter electrode (a)
- Standard electronic housing (a)

Intervention Bill:
- Gold working electrode with micro-patterned surface (a) - existing electrode modified with standard photolithography
- Hydrophobic self-assembled monolayer (OTS, octadecyltrichlorosilane) applied to patterned regions (b) - standard catalog material
- Hydrophilic self-assembled monolayer (PEG-Silane) applied to non-patterned regions (b) - standard catalog material
- Standard electronic housing (a)
- Standard Ag/AgCl reference electrode (a)
- Standard Pt counter electrode (a)

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
- Working electrode modification: same burden (photolithography is standard in electrode fabrication)
- Coating materials: same burden (OTS and PEG-Silane are commercially available standard materials)
- Additional processing steps: 2 extra steps (surface patterning and selective coating application), but these are standard microfabrication processes already in use for other components
- Overall burden: same class (standard microfabrication processes and materials, no new equipment required)

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Implant 20 sensors with the intervention and 20 standard sensors in a diabetic porcine model. Measure glucose concentration simultaneously using reference blood draws every 6 hours for 14 days. Calculate MARD (Mean Absolute Relative Difference) between sensor readings and reference values at each time point.

Instruments: Standard CGM sensors, reference blood glucose analyzer, data acquisition system.

Pass/Fail Threshold: Intervention group must maintain MARD <10% for the full 14-day period without recalibration. Control group is expected to exceed MARD >10% by day 7.

Duration: 14 days of continuous wear.

Kill Criterion: Any sensor showing MARD >15% at any time point is considered failed and the test is terminated for that sensor. The intervention passes if ≥90% of intervention sensors complete the 14-day period without exceeding MARD >10%.
